papers.title: Paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$: complete one phonon Raman spectrum
papers.abstract: In this study we present a complete first-order Raman scattering spectrum of paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$- a material, where new type of spin texture induced by noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the N\'eel temperature ($T_N \approx 90$ K) gives rise to unconventional scenario of magnetism. Basic properties of all five phonon modes ($A_g$, $E_g$ and three $T_g$) predicted by the group theory have been successfully approached through polarization, excitation and temperature dependent measurements. In particular, the ever-missing phonon mode of $T_g$ symmetry has been unambiguously resolved in the room temperature Raman spectrum at approximately 107 cm$^{-1}$, just 1.5 cm$^{-1}$ higher in frequency compared to the $E_g$ mode. Density functional theory calculations reproduce the observed Raman-active phonon spectrum and support the assignment of all five first-order Raman modes, including the near-degeneracy of the $E_g$ and one of the $T_g$ vibrations. The calculations further reveal a dense manifold of low-energy antiferromagnetic spin configurations, separated from the ground state by only a few meV per formula unit. Furthermore, strong signals of inelastically scattered light from the paramagnetic (PM) phase of MnTe$_2$ were acquired with long wavelength excitations, i.e. 633 nm and 785 nm, revealing the $2A_g$ overtone at approx. 360 cm$^{-1}$. The enhanced absorption of the light in the near infrared range could be a putative reason behind the anomalous angular dependence of scattered intensity of the highest frequency $T_g$ phonon mode (183 cm$^{-1}$) measured in PM MnTe$_2$ with parallelly aligned polarizers. Finally, upon cooling just below the $T_N$, the measured properties of phonons remained basically unperturbed by the incipient long-range antiferromagnetic ordering.

papers.title: Two quantum skyrmions form a magnon Josephson junction
papers.abstract: Two quantum skyrmions in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ magnet bind into a molecule, and the molecule acts as a magnon Josephson junction: the relative helicity $\theta$ and the number $n$ of magnons transferred between them obey $H=E_Cn^2-W\cos\theta$. DMRG on the $J_1$--$J_2$ triangular lattice gives $E_C$ as the curvature of the skyrmion energy at its natural size of seven flipped spins, and the measured helicity coherence fixes $W\simeq0.02J_1$, half the skyrmion--antiskyrmion tunnel splitting and independent of the anisotropy. Two helicity qubits side by side are thus strongly coupled by their own interaction.

papers.title: From Traveling Waves to Synthetic Gauge Fields: A Field-Free Route to Superconducting Diode Effect
papers.abstract: The superconducting diode effect requires the forward and reverse bias currents to differ, a scenario achieved via inversion and time-reversal symmetries broken together. The latter, and the more crucial one, is inevitably achieved by a magnetic field. Here, we show that a spatio-temporally driven chemical potential of the form, $\mu_j(t)=\mu+V\cos(\omega t+\kd j)$, achieves both at once. Applied to a helical Shiba chain, the drive transmutes a traveling Peierls phase via generating an odd-in-momentum term, equivalent to an imaginary next-nearest-neighbour Haldane-like hopping in real space. Remarkably, the protocol is spin-blind, which renders the time-reversal breaking via a synthetic gauge flux rather than an effective Zeeman field. The rectification is odd in the drive wavevector, with exact zeros at $\kd=n\pi$ and an analytical optimum at $\kd=2\pi/3$. It is however, even in the exchange coupling, $J$ and persists even at $J=0$. Furthermore, the rectification scales inversely with the pair-breaking gap, yielding approximately $50\%$ rectification in the topological phase and $10\%$ in the trivial phase. Symmetry breaking is thus drive-controlled, allowing it to be switched on, tuned, and reversed without an external magnetic field.

papers.title: Chiral near-fields at achiral plasmonic tips enable nanoscale valley polarimetry
papers.abstract: Optical helicity is central to chiral light-matter interactions, yet plasmonic confinement typically distorts it at the nanoscale. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale valley polarimetry using an achiral Au tip, where incidence-angle control of circularly polarized light creates a strongly localized, helicity-preserving near-field. Chiral tip-enhanced photoluminescence (c-TEPL) directly resolves and reverses local valley polarization in monolayer WSe2 and reveals nanoscale polarization variations in strained MoS2 hidden by diffraction-limited measurements.

papers.title: Tunable flat bands from a parent chiral Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Systems with flat bands are interesting as they potentially host many exotic quantum phenomena that would be hard to observe in usual systems with dispersive bands. Multiple approaches were developed to construct flat band systems, with most of them requiring fine-tuning and/or solving a challenging inverse-eigenvalue problem. In this article we work with an idea that uses a parent bipartite system to generate a family of flat bands by means of Hilbert space projections. This method is largely free from fine-tuning constraints and allows us to identify conditions for a Hamiltonian to guarantee flat bands at desired energies, with desired degree of degeneracy. We also show that one can control the touching points of the flat band with dispersive bands at any desirable point in the Brillouin zone. In the process, we identify perturbations that preserve the flat bands or split them controllably. This approach provides easy tunability in designing flat band systems with desired properties.

papers.title: Boundary exceptional point driven chiral switch of topological edge states
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries. By tuning the boundary gain and loss parameters, we exploit the finite-size hybridization of two mid-gap topological edge states to analytically derive the exact coordinates of boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs), $\Gamma_{\rm EP}=\pm i v^{N}/w^{N-1}$, at which these states undergo coalescence. We demonstrate that dynamically encircling these boundary EPs facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol. Depending on the orientation of the encircling loop, this protocol allows a topological edge state localized at one boundary to be either transferred to the opposite edge with perfect fidelity or returned to its starting position through a double switching process. Importantly, since the non-Hermiticity remains strictly confined to the boundaries, this chiral transport occurs without affecting the energy spectrum of the bulk bands. These results establish a minimal framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch that is experimentally verifiable and capable of being controlled through boundary non-Hermitian driving.

papers.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
papers.abstract: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

papers.title: Disorder-induced modal alignment in transmission eigenchannels enables control of wave transport
papers.abstract: The transmission eigenchannels of a disordered medium range from unity transmission and high internal energy density to vanishing transmission and low internal energy density. Although the transmission matrix underlies central ideas in mesoscopic electronic transport, it cannot be measured directly in electronic systems. For classical waves, however, the measurable matrix gives access to eigenchannels that control transmission and energy density within the medium. Coherence underlies transmission-eigenvalue scaling, the bimodal distribution in diffusive samples, and Anderson localization. What has remained unresolved is how interference among modal contributions is organized within individual eigenchannels throughout the sample. Here, microwave transmission-matrix measurements resolve the complex contribution of each incident mode to every transmitted mode of each eigenchannel. In simulations, we construct a flux matrix that generalizes the transmission matrix to every depth and further separate each internal modal contribution into forward- and backward-propagating components. For each eigenchannel, the directional flux in every mode throughout the sample factorizes into the squared modal amplitudes of the incident eigenchannel, coupling between waveguide modes, and modal alignment. In high-transmission eigenchannels, the contributions align increasingly constructively with depth, approaching nearly perfect alignment in the highest channel near the localization crossover. In low-transmission eigenchannels, contributions interfere destructively, producing vanishing transmission at a transmission zero. Because the contributions remain appreciable as their coherent sum approaches zero, transmission far below the noise floor of conventional transmission measurements can be determined.

papers.title: Microscopic study of topological phase transitions: Percolation point of view
papers.abstract: We investigate microscopic mechanisms underlying decoherence-induced transitions between topologically ordered states. As a first case study, we analyze the color code using topological entanglement negativity (TEN) and a disorder parameter associated with 1-form symmetry. We interpret these quantities as first- and zeroth-dimensional simplicial homological objects, respectively, and show that the transition can be understood in terms of decoherence percolation. To resolve its local structure, we introduce quasi-local TEN (QLTEN), which visualizes the spatial distribution of local topological properties and the growth of decohered regions. We further introduce explosive percolation (EP), corresponding here to biased decoherence that suppresses the formation of large decohered clusters. As a second case study, we consider the toric code on a triangular lattice under external-field-type decoherence. Numerical results show that QLTEN faithfully captures the emergence of Higgs regions and the survival of logical qubits. Although global TEN, QLTEN clusters, and string operators are strongly correlated in both models, the color code and toric code respond differently to EP patterns. This difference indicates that a universal microscopic description of decoherence-induced topological phase transitions remains challenging even for closely related systems.

papers.title: Discrete semiclassical theory of quantum-thermal escape
papers.abstract: The dissipationless quantum-thermal escape rate from a metastable well is often written as a Boltzmann average of the Hill-Wheeler flux over a continuum of energies. This continuum treatment diverges exponentially at low temperature, because it pairs the quantum partition function of the well with a classical flux integral. Retaining the discrete nature of the quasibound spectrum removes the divergence exactly, and the resulting rate is obtained in closed form on both sides of the crossover temperature $T_0$. Evaluating a uniform Kemble transmission probability on Bohr-Sommerfeld levels further removes the parabolic-barrier error and recovers the WKB decay rate of the lowest resonance at zero temperature. Benchmarked against the resonances of cubic and quintic potentials, obtained by complex scaling, this uniform semiclassical rate stays within $9\%$ of the exact one over eleven orders of magnitude. Below $T_0$, the rate rises above its zero-temperature plateau with the level spacing as activation energy, and the plateau ends at a temperature $T_1$ noticeably below $T_0$. In an isolated well, whose levels are not replenished, the thermal rate is only the initial slope of a decay which ceases to be single exponential at $T_1$, while at $T_0$ the initial escape moves from tunneling inside the well to the barrier top. We discuss implications for Josephson junctions, single-electron pumps, and nuclear burning in dense stellar matter.
